headline: Argentine ADRs Drop Up to 61% YTD on Wall Street Amid Elevated Country Risk
summary: US-listed shares of Argentine companies fell up to 61% year-to-date as rising country risk metrics and foreign exchange volatility pressured domestic equities.
why: Argentine ADRs serve as a primary vehicle for international institutional exposure to South American emerging market sovereign risk and corporate balance sheets.

impacts.name: Argentina
impacts.why: Global risk aversion and elevated sovereign risk metrics triggered heavy equity selling.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Foreign exchange pressure and rising country risk spreads drove broad capital flight from Argentine shares.
